sections.heading: Delimiter Detection and Manual Override
paragraphs: CSV files exported from different regions use different delimiters: commas in the United States, semicolons in much of Europe and tabs in many developer tools.
The converter attempts automatic delimiter detection by analyzing the first few rows for consistent field counts, but manual override is always available when the heuristic guesses wrong.
Choosing the correct delimiter is the single most important step for clean conversion, because a mismatch causes entire rows to collapse into a single field.
Once the delimiter is set, the preview updates immediately so you can confirm the column structure before generating the final JSON output.

sections.heading: Type Inference: Numbers, Booleans and Nulls
paragraphs: Raw CSV text treats every cell as a string, but JSON benefits from proper typing so that downstream code can perform numeric comparisons and boolean logic without additional parsing.
The converter inspects each cell and promotes values that look like numbers into JSON number types, recognizes true and false as booleans, and converts empty or explicitly null cells to null.
Strings that happen to contain numeric characters but have leading zeros or special formatting are preserved as strings to avoid data loss.
This type-aware conversion means the resulting JSON array is immediately usable in applications that expect correctly typed values without post-processing.

sections.heading: Handling Multiline Fields and Embedded Commas
paragraphs: Real CSV exports frequently contain fields wrapped in quotation marks that span multiple lines or include commas within the text content.
The converter follows RFC 4180 rules for quoted fields, correctly identifying field boundaries even when newlines or delimiters appear inside the quotes.
This behavior mirrors how professional spreadsheet applications export data, ensuring that your conversion handles the same files without manual cleanup.
Fields that contain escaped quotes are unescaped properly, so the JSON output reflects the intended content rather than the raw escape sequences.

sections.heading: Output Formatting Options
paragraphs: Compact JSON output minimizes file size for API payloads and configuration files where whitespace adds no value.
Pretty-printed output with consistent indentation makes the JSON readable for debugging, code review and manual inspection.
The converter lets you choose between these formats so the downloaded file matches the conventions of your project.
Choosing the right format at conversion time saves a separate formatting step later in the workflow.

sections.heading: Batch Conversion and Automation Workflows
paragraphs: Teams that convert CSV data regularly benefit from establishing a consistent process: paste, configure delimiter, preview and download.
Because the conversion runs entirely in the browser, it integrates naturally into bookmarklet workflows and local automation scripts that pipe data through the tool.
Repeatability matters when the same source file is updated weekly; the settings you choose today can be reapplied manually to future exports.
For developers building pipelines, the predictable JSON structure produced by the converter simplifies the schema validation step that follows data ingestion.

faqs.q: How are CSV columns mapped to JSON?
faqs.a: When the first row contains headers, each later row becomes an object keyed by those column names; other rows become array items.

faqs.q: Does the converter handle quoted commas within fields?
faqs.a: Yes. Quoted fields containing commas or newlines are parsed correctly according to CSV rules.
Yes. Everything runs locally in your browser with no uploads or accounts.

faqs.q: Can the converter detect the delimiter automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. It analyzes the first rows for consistent field counts, though manual override is available when the automatic detection does not match your file.

faqs.q: Are numeric values preserved as numbers in the JSON?
faqs.a: Yes. Cells that contain valid numbers are promoted to JSON number types, while values with leading zeros or special formatting remain as strings.
